Overview

The Challenge

Build an AI agent that lives in a git repo. Define it using the gitagent standard, bring it to life with gitclaw, and optionally deploy it serverlessly with clawless.

Join discord and build together gitAgent Discord

How It Works

Step 1: Define Your Agent (gitagent format)

Create a git repo with this structure:

my-agent/
├── agent.yaml # Manifest: name, version, description, skills, model
├── SOUL.md # Who your agent is — personality, values, expertise
├── RULES.md # What your agent must/must never do
├── skills/
│ └── my-skill/
│ └── SKILL.md # A capability with YAML frontmatter + instructions
└── tools/ # Optional: tool definitions (YAML schemas)

agent.yaml — the manifest:

spec_version: "0.1.0"
name: my-hackathon-agent
version: 0.1.0
description: "What your agent does in one line"
model:
preferred: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929
skills:
- my-skill
tags:
- hackathon

SOUL.md — your agent's identity:

# Soul

## Core Identity
I am a [role]. I specialize in [domain].

## Communication Style
[How your agent talks, thinks, responds]

## Values
- [What matters to your agent]

RULES.md — hard constraints:

# Rules

## Must Always
- [Non-negotiable behaviors]

## Must Never
- [Hard boundaries]

skills/my-skill/SKILL.md — a capability:

---
name: my-skill
description: "What this skill does"
allowed-tools: Bash Read Write
---

# My Skill

Instructions for how the agent should execute this skill.

Validate your agent:

npx gitagent validate
npx gitagent info

Step 2: Build Your Agent (gitclaw SDK)

Use gitclaw to turn your repo into a running agent:

npm install gitclaw

gitclaw reads your gitagent repo and creates a fully functional AI agent — with the identity from SOUL.md, rules from RULES.md, skills from skills/, and tools from tools/. Your agent definition is the git repo. gitclaw is the runtime.

See the gitclaw README for full SDK docs, examples, and API reference.

Step 3 (Optional): Deploy Serverlessly (clawless)

Want your agent running in the browser with zero infrastructure? Use clawless — a serverless runtime powered by WebContainers.

npm install clawless

Important: clawless runs in a WebContainer environment with Node.js/npm only. Your agent's skills and tools must be Node-compatible. No Python, no system binaries, no Docker. If your skill runs node or npx, it works. If it needs python or apt-get, use gitclaw instead.

See the clawless README for setup, deployment, and limitations.

Judging Criteria

CriteriaWeightWhat We're Looking For
Agent Quality30%Does the agent do something useful? Is the SOUL.md compelling? Are the rules well-defined?
Skill Design25%Are skills focused, well-documented, and practical? Do they follow the SKILL.md standard?
Working Demo25%Does it actually run via gitclaw or clawless? Can we see it in action?
Creativity20%Surprise us. Novel use cases, clever skill compositions, unexpected domains.

Quick Reference: gitagent CLI

npx gitagent init # Scaffold a new agent
npx gitagent validate # Validate your agent
npx gitagent info # Show agent summary
npx gitagent export -f system-prompt # Preview as system prompt
npx gitagent export -f claude-code # Export for Claude Code
npx gitagent export -f cursor # Export for Cursor

Build something great. Your agent is a git repo. Make it count.

Rules

Dates

  • Hackathon opens: 23rd March
  • Submissions close: 10th April
  • Winners announced: 20th April

Eligibility

  • Open to participants worldwide
  • Solo Participants only
  • Lyzr employees and organizers are not eligible for prizes

Project & Submission Requirements

  • Projects must use or extend the GitAgent open standard
  • All code must be open source and in a public GitHub repository
  • Projects must be built during the hackathon window — no prior work
  • A working demo or prototype is required at time of submission

FAQs

No. gitagent is model-agnostic. Set model.preferred in agent.yaml to whatever you want - Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama, etc. gitclaw handles the runtime.

Yes. Add as many as you want under skills/. Each gets its own directory with a SKILL.md file.

Yes. Add them under agents/ — each sub-agent is a full gitagent directory with its own agent.yaml, SOUL.md, etc.

Use gitclaw (not clawless). clawless only supports Node.js/npm environments. gitclaw has no such limitation.

Yes. gitagent import --from claude <path> or gitagent import --from cursor <path> converts existing configs to gitagent format.
